QuestionStmt.S: In Young's double slit experiment, the distance between screen and aperture is 1 m. The slit width is 2 mm. Light of 6000Å is used. If a thin glass plate ($\mu = 1.5$) of thickness 0.04 mm is placed over one of the slits, then there will be a lateral displacement of the fringes by

Solution.S:
The lateral displacement of fringes when a thin glass plate is placed over one slit is given by:
$$d' = \frac{t(\mu - 1)D}{d}$$
where $t$ = thickness of plate, $\mu$ = refractive index, $D$ = distance from slits to screen, $d$ = slit separation.

Given: $t = 0.04 \text{ mm} = 0.04 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, $\mu = 1.5$, $D = 1 \text{ m}$, $d = 2 \text{ mm} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.

$$d' = \frac{0.04 \times 10^{-3} \times (1.5 - 1) \times 1}{2 \times 10^{-3}}$$
$$= \frac{0.04 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.5}{2 \times 10^{-3}} = \frac{0.02 \times 10^{-3}}{2 \times 10^{-3}} = 0.01 \text{ m} = 1 \text{ cm}$$

Thus the lateral displacement is 1 cm, which corresponds to option B.
